question.text:
Consider the following statements about a property eligible for reverse mortgage:
1. The property must have a residual life of at least 20 years 2. The property can be a commercial property (e.g., a shop or office) provided the borrower owns it 3. The property must be free from any encumbrance 4. The maximum monthly payment under reverse mortgage is capped at Rs. 50,000
Which of the above statements are correct?

explanation.text: The Logic: Statement 1 is correct - the property must have a residual life of at least 20 years. Statement 2 is INCORRECT - per the workbook (pp. 118-119), reverse mortgage cannot be availed against commercial property; the property must be a residential property (house or flat) used as the borrower's permanent primary residence. Statement 3 is correct - the property must be free from encumbrance. Statement 4 is correct - the maximum monthly payment is capped at Rs. 50,000. Hence 1, 3 and 4 are correct (option B). The Trap: Statement 2 is the false statement the question is built around; candidates who incorrectly assume commercial ownership qualifies will include it. The "all four correct" distractor (option C) tempts students who treat every plausible-sounding statement as true. Note: The original statement 2 referred to a farmhouse used as a primary residence, but the workbook does not expressly exclude farmhouses, only commercial property - so flagging statement 2 as false was not source-grounded. Statement 2 has been rewritten to assert eligibility of commercial property, which the workbook expressly contradicts, so the keyed answer (1, 3, 4 correct) is uniquely supported. Source: NISM Series-X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook, pp. 118-119.
